column4: The exact same three-quarter side view of this porcelain maid on the same flat ivory paper, same pose, hair, dress, scale and position. One fix only: there must be NOTHING beside her hair at shoulder height; delete the floating key there completely and fill that area with plain paper and hair. Her wind-up key is mounted lower, on her back at the height of the white apron waist bow: a short straight coal shaft comes out of her back just above the bow and points backward, away from her body, and the key's two round loops sit at the end of that shaft, upright, behind her waist, partly overlapping her long hair. The second reference shows where the mount sits on her back.

The exact same cathedral interior, same camera, same pews and the same hooded congregants in exactly the same positions and sizes as the reference. Every figure keeps its deep coal hood fully on; no faces, no heads or hair are revealed. Change only the posture: every hooded figure has tilted its head far back to look up at the stage and the high window, so each hood now points steeply upward, its peak tipped backward and the dark hood opening facing up toward the window, with the line of the neck stretched up. The change from bowed hoods to upturned hoods must be obvious in every row.
